publicHistory.title: Public History
publicHistory.short: Work exploring how history is communicated and remembered
publicHistory.desc: Public History explores how the past is communicated, interpreted, and experienced beyond academia. Its practices span museums and exhibitions, journalism, digital media, performance, and other public settings. This section brings together work focusing particularly on documentary theatre and historical drama, and on how performance represents the past and shapes collective memory.

aboutText: The process of bringing a story to the stage, and the contexts behind it, are at the heart of this work. It follows the thoughts and choices of the people who create performances, as well as the stories and questions that emerge on stage, documenting and interpreting them through writing.

This interest also extends to history and memory. Through studies in Public History in Germany, the focus turns to how performance represents the past and shapes collective memory. Particular attention is given to why some histories are retold on stage while others remain outside it, and to stories that have been documented but not remembered.
